temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Thin fillets, tilapia or sole 400°F / 205°C · 7 min 425°F / 220°C · 9 min Standard fillets, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) 400°F / 205°C · 10 min 425°F / 220°C · 13 min Thick loins of cod or haddock 400°F / 205°C · 13 min 425°F / 220°C · 16 min Stuck to the basket, broken on the turn White fish has big, loose flakes held together by very little fat or connective tissue. Once it is cooked those flakes separate at a touch, which is the texture you want on the plate and the reason it falls apart on the way there. Bare fillets also stick to the mesh, because the proteins on the underside bond to hot metal before they firm up. Trying to flip a fillet halfway is where most go wrong: it tears, leaves its underside on the basket and ends up as pieces. So do not flip it. The circulating air cooks the top and the heat of the basket cooks the bottom well enough for fillets of normal thickness. Cook it on a sheet of perforated parchment or an oiled liner and lift the whole sheet out at the end. Worked example Two 6 oz cod fillets about an inch thick, patted dry, brushed with melted butter and topped with lemon zest and paprika. Preheat 4 minutes, set them on perforated parchment and cook at 400°F for 10 minutes without turning. Thin tilapia needs about 7 minutes and a thick cod loin about 13. In a conventional oven the same fillets take 425°F for around 13 minutes. How to tell it is done Press the thickest point gently with a fork: cooked white fish turns from translucent to bright, opaque white and separates into moist flakes. The safe internal temperature is 145°F (63°C). Thin fillets go from done to dry quickly, so check two minutes before the time. If the flakes look chalky and dry at the edges, the fish has gone too far. Before it goes in Thaw frozen fillets fully in the fridge and dry them well, since thawed fish carries a lot of water. Tuck any thin tail under so the fillet is an even thickness. Fat on top helps colour and flavour: a little butter, oil or mayonnaise mixed with herbs. For a crumb coating, press panko onto the top only. About 10 minutes at 400°F for inch-thick fillets of cod or haddock, without flipping. Thin tilapia takes around 7 minutes and thick loins around 13. Do I need to flip fish in the air fryer? No. Delicate fillets break when turned, and the hot air cooks the top well enough on its own. How do I stop fish sticking to the air fryer basket? Cook it on perforated parchment or an oiled liner and lift the sheet out. Patting the fish dry and oiling the underside helps too. What temperature is cooked cod? 145°F (63°C) at the thickest point, when the flesh is opaque and flakes easily. What is the oven equivalent for white fish? 425°F for around 13 minutes in a conventional oven, or 400°F for 11 minutes in a fan oven.
